specAnchors.text: know and use the relationship between voltage, current and resistance: voltage = current × resistance V = I × R

primer.text: Every component, even a plain copper wire, pushes back a little against the current trying to pass through it. That push-back is resistance. This note defines the ohm, shows how resistance throttles the current at a fixed voltage, and assembles the equation linking voltage, current and resistance that solves most simple circuits.

modules.title: Calculating current, resistance & potential difference
modules.opening: Squeeze a garden hose and the flow drops; leave it open and the flow soars. Resistance does to charge exactly what your hand does to the water. This lesson defines the ohm, sets the see-saw between resistance and current, and assembles the equation V = I × R that ties all three quantities together.
keyPoints: Resistance describes how strongly a component opposes the flow of current through it.
Resistance is measured in ohm units (Ω); one ohm lets one volt drive one amp through a component.
For a fixed voltage, a higher resistance means a smaller current, and a lower resistance means a larger one.
The three quantities are linked by V = I × R.
Copper wiring has a very low resistance, which is why it counts as a good conductor.
In exam circuits the wires, ammeters and cells are taken to have zero resistance.

low.restatement: Resistance is the brake on the current: more ohms means less flow for the same push.
low.analogy: A narrow door in a busy corridor — the wider the door (lower resistance), the more people (current) get through.
low.examPointer: Use Ω for ohms in your working, and keep V, A and Ω labelled in every substitution.

medium.restatement: The equation is a see-saw: at fixed voltage, current and resistance move in opposite directions, because I = V ÷ R.
medium.analogy: A credit limit: the voltage is your budget, the resistance is the price of goods, and the current is how much you can buy.
medium.examPointer: Assume wires, ammeters and cells have zero resistance unless a question says otherwise — only the named components count.

glossary.definition: The opposition a component offers to the current trying to flow through it, measured in ohms.
The unit of resistance — one volt driving one amp through the component.
A material that lets charge flow through it easily.
The rate at which electric charge streams through a component, measured in amperes.
The low-resistance metal usually chosen for connecting wires.

workedExample.prompt: Find the voltage across a 10 Ω resistor carrying a current of 0.3 A.
steps: List the knowns: resistance R = 10 Ω and current I = 0.3 A.
State the linking equation: V = I × R.
workedExample.finalAnswer: The voltage across the resistor is 3 V.
